findings.title: Existing symlink or hard link at a report/failures/summary/preflight file name in an allowed --output directory overwrites original fixtures; for the three files written after the hash check, the run exits 0 and reports file_hashes_unchanged: true
findings.repro:
Scripts: /tmp/qa-7b3/work/alias-guard/repro-output-alias.sh {sym|hard} and repro-preflight-alias.sh. Each makes a fresh copy (services/, packages/, pyproject.toml, tests/fixtures/memory) with the normal, non-symlinked fixture layout. Core steps: mkdir $D/out; ln [-s] $F/records.json $D/out/report.json; ln [-s] $F/labels.json $D/out/failures.json; ln [-s] $F/queries.json $D/out/summary.json; then from the copy run $PY -m services.learning.evaluate --output $D/out. The output dir resolves outside tests/fixtures/memory, so derived_path allows it. Output (identical for sym and hard):
BEFORE: files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=[] extra=[] MATCH=True
exit=0
"file_hashes_unchanged": true
AFTER:  files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=['labels.json', 'queries.json', 'records.json'] extra=[] MATCH=False
records.json now starts with {   "task": "P0-05",   "created_at": ...
Preflight variant (ln -s $F/README.md $D/out/preflight.json):
exit=1
AssertionError: Preservation or reproducibility regression
AFTER: changed_or_missing=['README.md'] MATCH=False
With preflight.json aliased to manifest.json (sym or hard), the original manifest is lost and the child restart probe fails with CalledProcessError, exit 1.
findings.expected: Derived --output files should never write through to original fixture bytes. Possible fixes: write each output through temp+os.replace so the name is replaced rather than the target, or refuse existing output entries that are symlinks, have st_nlink>1, or share a (st_dev, st_ino) with any fixture file. Do the final preservation check after all four outputs are written.
findings.actual: evaluate() writes all four outputs in place with write_bytes/write_text, which opens with O_TRUNC and follows symlinks and hard links. report/failures/summary are written after the before/after hashes(FIXTURES) comparison, so 3 of the 187 originals were overwritten and the run still exited 0. It printed and recorded preservation.file_hashes_unchanged=true, which is false. preflight.json is written before the check, so that alias is caught only after the original is already destroyed. The originals are not restored. Plausibility: this needs a link already present in the output dir. The default --output is a fixed shared path, /tmp/p005-evaluation, created with mkdir(exist_ok=True). I did not exercise that path. fs.protected_symlinks=1 does not cover files inside a non-sticky subdirectory owned by another user. Could be rated low if pre-planted links are considered contrived.

findings.title: If a non-manifest fixture file is itself a symlink, its literal in-tree path passes the guard and --restart-probe replaces the physical original (exit 0)
findings.repro:
Script /tmp/qa-7b3/work/alias-guard/repro-infile-link.sh. In a fresh copy: mv $F/labels.json $D/store/labels.json; ln -s $D/store/labels.json $F/labels.json; then from the copy run $PY -m services.learning.evaluate --restart-probe tests/fixtures/memory/labels.json. Output:
BEFORE: checked=187 changed_or_missing=[] MATCH=True
{"signature": "b5922ddd8314665e09498c795fc11763f727c126e0a791be3d01d432be157a46"}
exit=0
AFTER:  checked=187 changed_or_missing=['labels.json'] MATCH=False
The physical labels.json now starts with {"archive_fingerprint":"d901387a7b8ab24c. The same happened with --restart-probe $D/store/labels.json (the physical target path), exit 0.
findings.expected: A destination whose unresolved, parent-resolved name lies inside the fixture root should be rejected, as should one whose fully resolved target does. Ideally the guard would also reject any destination that is the same file as any fixture file.
findings.actual: derived_path fully resolves the final path component and checks only the resolved target. A per-file symlink therefore makes a literal tests/fixtures/memory/<name> path look like it is outside the fixture root. This only works for the 7 files not listed in manifest['files']: README.md, build_fixture.py, dev_queries.json, evaluation_spec.py, labels.json, manifest.json, queries.json. I tested only labels.json. For the 180 manifest-listed files, the same per-file or subdirectory symlink layout makes FixtureArchive.load fail closed with 'Fixture path leaves root' before any save. That fail-closed case is listed under held checks. Severity is low because only these specific non-manifest files can be symlinked out while the archive still loads.

findings.title: Nothing outside tests/fixtures/memory is protected: --restart-probe silently replaces any existing non-index file, including source code and committed evidence, and --output can overwrite the committed p0-05-time-fix comparison baseline
findings.repro:
Script /tmp/qa-7b3/work/alias-guard/repro-nonfixture.sh. It uses a fresh copy plus a copy of docs/verification/learning, then runs: $PY -m services.learning.evaluate --output docs/verification/learning/p0-05-time-fix; ... --restart-probe docs/verification/learning/p0-05-index-durability.json; ... --restart-probe services/learning/retrieval.py. Output:
--output evidence dir exit=0
{"signature": "b5922ddd..."} exit=0
{"signature": "b5922ddd..."} exit=0
p0-05-time-fix/comparison.json: OK
p0-05-time-fix/failures.json: FAILED
p0-05-time-fix/preflight.json: FAILED
p0-05-time-fix/report.json: FAILED
p0-05-time-fix/summary.json: FAILED
p0-05-index-durability.json: FAILED
services/learning/retrieval.py: FAILED
-rw------- (retrieval.py mode is now 0600)
AttributeError: module 'services.learning.retrieval' has no attribute 'RetrievalIndex'
fixtures: files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=[] extra=[] MATCH=True
findings.expected: Not claimed either way. The reports claim protection only for the 187 fixture originals. Suggested hardening: a 'probe' CLI should not replace an existing file that is not a recognizable prior index, for example by refusing existing files whose envelope is not an index or that are outside a designated cache directory. It could also refuse --output into repo-tracked evidence and source trees, or at least into directories that already contain these output names.
findings.actual: load_or_rebuild treats any unparsable or invalid existing file as a stale cache. It rebuilds and os.replace()s the file with index JSON, exits 0, and changes the file mode to 0600 because of NamedTemporaryFile. One mistaken argument to a command named like a read-only probe destroyed the retrieval implementation and the machine evidence JSON. evaluate --output also overwrote 4 of the 5 committed baseline files that later reports compare against. Fixtures were unchanged. Git can restore committed files, but uncommitted work at that path would be lost.
findings.owner: learning (services/learning/evaluate.py, retrieval.py load_or_rebuild); lead to decide whether a claim/guard is wanted

findings.title: Guard compares paths case-sensitively; case-variant fixture paths are accepted (likely overwrite on case-insensitive APFS, needs macOS verification)
findings.repro:
Guard-level reproduction, from the copy /tmp/qa-7b3/work/alias-guard/paths/proj: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 $PY -c "from pathlib import Path; import services.learning.evaluate as ev; print(ev.derived_path(Path('tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json')))". Output:
tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json -> ACCEPTED as .../proj/tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json
tests/Fixtures/memory/records.json -> ACCEPTED as .../proj/tests/Fixtures/memory/records.json
(tests/fixtures/memory/RECORDS.json -> rejected, because the root prefix still matches). CLI on this case-sensitive tmpfs, copy case-linux: --restart-probe tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json -> FileNotFoundError: .../tests/fixtures/MEMORY/.records.json.vjjnn4ja.tmp, exit=1, fixtures 187/187 MATCH. I could not reproduce end to end: the kernel has CONFIG_UNICODE unset, so tmpfs casefold is unavailable, and /mnt/c is outside my allowed scratch area.
findings.expected: On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS default), a case variant of the fixture root should be rejected. Possible fix: compare (st_dev, st_ino) of the destination's parent directories and target against the fixture root and fixture files, rather than comparing path strings.
findings.actual: Path.resolve() on POSIX, including macOS, does not canonicalize letter case, and is_relative_to compares case-sensitively. On a case-insensitive volume, tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json would name the real original. Load would fail validation, then rebuild, then os.replace over records.json. The same applies to --output tests/fixtures/MEMORY, but only for colliding names; the fixture root has no report/preflight/summary/failures files. ROOT also takes the case the user typed for cwd. Status: needs macOS or real-device verification; not demonstrated as an overwrite here.
findings.owner: learning (services/learning/evaluate.py); macOS verification by QA/iOS machine owner

findings.title: TOCTOU between derived_path() and the eventual write (note only, not exercised)
findings.repro: Not run, per the task. Static reading: restart_probe resolves once, then FixtureArchive.load, then load_or_rebuild, then NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent) and os.replace on the resolved path string. evaluate() resolves at the start but writes report/failures/summary only after two child-process restart probes and all scoring, a window of several seconds.
findings.expected: Not claimed. Concurrent or adversarial renames are outside the stated scope.
findings.actual: If a directory component of an allowed destination is swapped for a symlink into the fixture root after the check, the later open or os.replace would follow it. Opening the directory once and using dir_fd/O_NOFOLLOW would close this. Recorded as untested, together with the explicitly unclaimed directory fsync, power loss, distributed FS and concurrent writers.

verdicts.actual_output:
Fresh copies under /tmp/qa-7b3/work/verify-alias-guard/ag01-{sym,hard}. Script: /tmp/qa-7b3/work/verify-alias-guard/ag01.sh {sym|hard}. Hashes are checked against my own reference ref.txt, built from git blobs at 7b36ccb rather than the first reviewer's ref.json.
sym: BEFORE: files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=[] extra=[] MATCH=True / exit=0 / "file_hashes_unchanged": true / AFTER: files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=['labels.json', 'queries.json', 'records.json'] extra=[] MATCH=False / records.json starts {   "task": "P0-05",   "created_at": "2026-09-28T13:02:19.10
hard: the output is identical, including exit=0, file_hashes_unchanged true and the same three files changed. The links had st_nlink=2 before the run.
Preflight variant, script ag01b.sh {README.md|manifest.json} {sym|hard}: README.md sym and hard both gave exit=1 with AssertionError: Preservation or reproducibility regression, and AFTER changed_or_missing=['README.md']. manifest.json sym and hard both gave exit=1 with CalledProcessError from the child --restart-probe, and AFTER changed_or_missing=['manifest.json'].
verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly. This violates the tested claim that derived output never overwrites the 187 originals. evaluate() writes report.json, failures.json and summary.json at lines 156/158/161, after the before/after hashes() comparison at lines 130-141, so preservation.file_hashes_unchanged:true is recorded even though three originals were destroyed. The durability report's claim 'restart CLI guards originals, including symlink aliases' and the lead's 'closes the actual source-overwrite path' do not cover per-file links inside the output directory. Severity is inflated at medium, though. The attack needs someone to have deliberately pre-created a symlink or hard link with one of the four output names (report/failures/summary/preflight.json) pointing at a fixture file. The fixture root contains no files with those names, and no normal workflow creates such links, so this is a contrived setup. The only non-deliberate vector is a hostile local user pre-creating the shared default /tmp/p005-evaluation. I did not exercise that; the path does not currently exist, and that threat model is not claimed. So: defect, low. The false-true preservation field is worth fixing together with it. Moving the final hash check after all four writes and writing outputs via temp+os.replace would close both issues. Owner: learning (services/learning/evaluate.py).

verdicts.actual_output: Script: /tmp/qa-7b3/work/verify-alias-guard/ag02.sh NAME {literal|physical}. Each run uses a fresh copy with $F/NAME moved to $D/store/NAME and symlinked back into the fixture root. For labels.json, queries.json and README.md, both literal (tests/fixtures/memory/NAME) and physical ($D/store/NAME) gave: BEFORE: checked=187 changed_or_missing=[] MATCH=True / {"signature": "b5922ddd8314665e09498c795fc11763f727c126e0a791be3d01d432be157a46"} / exit=0 / AFTER: checked=187 changed_or_missing=['NAME'] MATCH=False. The link stays in place (lrwxrwxrwx) and the physical file now starts {"archive_fingerprint":"d901387a7b8ab24c33b62. I also confirmed that exactly 7 files are outside manifest['files']: README.md, build_fixture.py, dev_queries.json, evaluation_spec.py, labels.json, manifest.json, queries.json.
verdicts.reason: Reproduced for three of the seven non-manifest files. derived_path resolves the final component, so the literal in-tree path tests/fixtures/memory/labels.json passes the guard and the resolved target is replaced. The physical-path variant is effectively the AG-03 class: the target lies outside the root, and the guard cannot know it is an original without an identity check. The layout is contrived. Only non-manifest files can be linked out, because manifest-covered files fail closed with 'Fixture path leaves root', which I rechecked. Low severity is correct. Owner: learning.

verdicts.actual_output: Script: /tmp/qa-7b3/work/verify-alias-guard/ag03.sh, run on a fresh copy plus a copy of docs/verification/learning. BEFORE fixtures: files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=[] extra=[] MATCH=True; retrieval.py -rw-rw-r--. Results: '--output evidence dir exit=0'. --restart-probe docs/verification/learning/p0-05-index-durability.json gave the signature b5922ddd... with exit=0. --restart-probe services/learning/retrieval.py gave the same signature with exit=0. sha256sum -c: comparison.json OK; failures.json, preflight.json, report.json, summary.json, p0-05-index-durability.json and services/learning/retrieval.py all FAILED. retrieval.py is now -rw------- and importing it gives AttributeError: module 'services.learning.retrieval' has no attribute 'RetrievalIndex'. AFTER fixtures: files=187 ref=187 changed_or_missing=[] extra=[] MATCH=True.
verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly, but it is not claimed either way, and the durability report documents the limit ('The library expects a dedicated cache path'). No fixture original is affected, and the damaged files are git-tracked and restorable. The --output half should be reclassified as an observation: overwriting the four named outputs in a directory the user passes as --output is ordinary output-flag behavior. The --restart-probe half is a genuine hardening gap. load_or_rebuild treats any unparsable or non-index file as a stale cache and atomically replaces it with 0600 index JSON, exiting 0. That happens only when a cache-path argument is misused. So: gap, low, not medium. Owner: learning, with the lead deciding whether an explicit guard or claim is wanted.

verdicts.actual_output: Guard level, in copy /tmp/qa-7b3/work/verify-alias-guard/ag04/proj: tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json -> ACCEPTED .../proj/tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json. tests/Fixtures/memory/records.json -> ACCEPTED. TESTS/fixtures/memory -> ACCEPTED. tests/fixtures/memory/RECORDS.json -> rejected: Derived output cannot overwrite fixtures. On case-sensitive tmpfs the CLI gives FileNotFoundError: .../tests/fixtures/MEMORY/.records.json.r..., exit=1, fixtures 187/187 MATCH. I confirmed that casefold is unavailable here (# CONFIG_UNICODE is not set). stdlib posixpath.realpath, which macOS also uses, only calls lstat/readlink and never canonicalizes case. Simulation of a non-symlink alias with script ag04-bind.sh: unshare -rm plus mount --bind tests/fixtures/memory tests/fixtures/MEMORY, then --restart-probe tests/fixtures/MEMORY/records.json, gave BEFORE MATCH=True / {"signature": "b5922ddd..."} / exit=0 / AFTER changed_or_missing=['records.json'] MATCH=False, with records.json now starting {"archive_fingerprint":"d901387a7b8ab24c33b62.
verdicts.reason: The guard does accept case variants, and the bind-mount simulation shows the full chain once any non-symlink alias passes the string comparison: guard passes, archive loads, validation fails, rebuild, then os.replace over the original. The same chain applies to container dual mounts and macOS firmlinks. However, I could not reproduce an overwrite on a real case-insensitive filesystem, and triggering it needs a wrong-case path that also points at a fixture destination. Severity is therefore low, pending macOS/APFS verification. If APFS verification confirms an overwrite, medium would be justified, for example with an absolute path built from a shell $PWD that kept the user's typed case while Python's getcwd-derived ROOT is canonical. An identity-based check ((st_dev, st_ino) of parent directories and target) would cover all of these alias classes. Status: needs macOS verification.

verdicts.actual_output: Not executed; this is by design and out of scope. Static reading of evaluate.py at exact commit 7b36ccb confirms the description. derived_path resolves once (lines 45 and 80). restart_probe then does FixtureArchive.load and load_or_rebuild, and save uses NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent) plus os.replace on the path string, with no dir_fd or O_NOFOLLOW. evaluate() writes preflight at line 101 and report/failures/summary at lines 156-161, after two batches of child processes.
verdicts.reason: The static description is accurate. TOCTOU/concurrent races fall under the explicitly unclaimed concurrency scope, so this stays an informational observation and is recorded as untested, not as a defect.

findings.title: evaluate --output writes report files through pre-existing symlink or hardlink entries into fixture originals; exits 0 and says hashes are unchanged
findings.repro: Setup (scratch copy only): W=/tmp/qa-7b3/work/snapshot-recovery; P=$W/proj2; mkdir -p $P/tests/fixtures; cp -r /tmp/qa-7b3/repo/{services,packages,pyproject.toml} $P/; cp -r /tmp/qa-7b3/repo/tests/fixtures/memory $P/tests/fixtures/memory; cd $P; export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=$P TMPDIR=$W/tmp. Symlink variant: O=$W/runs/entry-out; mkdir -p $O; ln -s $P/tests/fixtures/memory/labels.json $O/summary.json; /tmp/qa-7b3/repo/.venv/bin/python -m services.learning.evaluate --output $O. Hardlink variant: O=$W/runs/entry-out-hl; mkdir -p $O; ln $P/tests/fixtures/memory/queries.json $O/failures.json; same command. Cause: derived_path() (evaluate.py:36-41) checks only the output directory. write_bytes/write_text (evaluate.py:101,156,158,161) follow symlinks and truncate the shared inode in place. The after=hashes(FIXTURES) check (line 130) runs before report.json, failures.json and summary.json are written.
findings.expected: No --output invocation overwrites any of the 187 originals. The command either refuses or replaces the directory entry atomically.
